subtype: Being the subject of office talk [Receiver]
passage:
Farhan caught me at the lift, quietly, like he was handing over a parcel. “People are saying you got the senior role because you're close to the director, and that you and Meera from finance are together.” I laughed it off, but by afternoon I could feel it: the pantry going quiet, eyes sliding away. I'm Nitin, by the way.

For two weeks I arrived at eight, wore my sharpest shirt and never left before the director did, just so nobody could say I was slacking. I stopped talking to Meera altogether. It was exhausting. I spent more energy on what they thought than on my actual work. One evening Sanjay, who never gossips, said, “You look tired, man. Are you okay?” And I nearly cried.

qa.q: Where did Farhan tell Nitin what people were saying?
qa.a: Farhan caught Nitin at the lift and quietly said what people were saying about the senior role.

qa.q: Why did Nitin start arriving at eight and never leave before the director?
qa.a: Nitin felt anxious and watched after hearing the rumours, so managing the impression that nobody could call Nitin a slacker became more urgent than the actual work.

qa.q: What did Sanjay do that helped Nitin near the end?
qa.a: Sanjay, who never gossips, asked if Nitin was okay, which let Nitin drop the act and nearly cry.

qa.q: What might Meera feel after Nitin stopped talking to Meera altogether?
qa.a: Meera might feel confused, hurt and unfairly dragged into the talk.

grounding: An employee finds out that people at work speculate about their promotion and personal life, feels exposed and over-manages their image.

subtype: Being the subject of office talk [Receiver]
passage:
I'm Sarika, and I sit behind Jagdish on the accounts floor. Last month the talk started. Why does he leave at five sharp on Thursdays? Is there someone? Did the promotion come from a friend upstairs? Nobody said it to his face, but he heard. I saw his shoulders change.

The next week Jagdish came in at eight, stopped leaving at five and straightened his tie whenever the manager walked by. He skipped lunch invitations so nobody could ask questions. I can't say what he was feeling. He looked like someone on a stage. Pooja from payroll, who had started half of it, kept glancing at him and then at her screen. I nearly told her to stop, but I didn't. I'm still not sure Jagdish knows I noticed.

qa.q: At what time does Jagdish leave on Thursdays?
qa.a: Jagdish leaves at five sharp on Thursdays.

qa.q: Why does Jagdish skip lunch invitations and straighten the tie when the manager walks by?
qa.a: Jagdish feels exposed and is managing how others see Jagdish, hoping nobody will ask questions or find more to talk about.

qa.q: What small step could Sarika take next that helps Jagdish without adding to the talk?
qa.a: Sarika could speak to Jagdish privately and kindly, making clear Sarika is not part of the talk.

qa.q: What might Pooja be feeling, glancing at Jagdish and then at the screen?
qa.a: Pooja may feel uneasy or guilty about having started the talk, but not brave enough to stop it.

grounding: An observer on the same floor sees an employee who learns that coworkers speculate about their life and promotion, and who begins over-managing their image.
